question.text: Under SEBI regulations, an Infrastructure Debt Fund (IDF) mutual fund scheme can be set up ONLY as:

answer.text: A closed-ended debt scheme investing primarily in debt securities of infrastructure companies or infrastructure capital companies
An interval fund with quarterly redemption windows
An exchange-traded fund tracking an infrastructure index

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p54), an Infrastructure Debt Fund (IDF) under the mutual fund framework is set up as a close-ended scheme that invests primarily — minimum 90% of its scheme assets — in debt or securitised debt instruments of infrastructure companies, infrastructure projects or SPVs. The Trap: IDF is a debt product, not equity (Option A), and must be close-ended rather than open-ended or interval (Options A and C). An infrastructure ETF tracking an equity index is a different category and not what the IDF-MF framework prescribes. Note: The 90% scheme-assets floor in infrastructure debt is the regulatory feature that anchors the IDF-MF category — without it, the close-ended debt vehicle would not qualify as an IDF.
